title: Complete summary – MSK: techniques, anatomy & semiology
html:
Built by reverse-engineering every MCQ of this lecture. 🔁 = asked in several sessions · ⚠ = classic trap.

Bone tissue

  • Organic matrix ≈ 35 % (collagen), inorganic ≈ 65 % (hydroxyapatite, water).
  • Osteoblasts build bone, osteoclasts resorb it.

Choosing the technique

  • First imaging of the skeleton: radiography in two perpendicular views. Then CT (complex fractures, cortex, sequestrum), MRI (marrow, soft tissues).
  • MRI superior for: bone marrow oedema, articular cartilage, ligaments & menisci, early osteonecrosis, early sacroiliitis. CT best for cortical detail.
  • MSK ultrasound – advantages: non-invasive, non-ionising, repeatable, direct soft-tissue assessment, dynamic, guidance. Limits (= NOT advantages): operator-dependent, needs specific training ⚠

Changes in bone size – vocabulary 🔁🔁

TermMeaning
HyperostosisTHICKER bone
HypostosisTHINNER bone
Anostosisabsence of a bone
Osteosclerosischange of STRUCTURE (↑ density), not of size ⚠

Changes in bone structure

  • Osteoporosis = loss of mineral content with normal protein matrix → ↑ transparency.
  • Osteolysis patterns: geographic (well-defined), moth-eaten, permeative (most aggressive). Ivory / snowball = osteosclerosis.

Osteoporosis on radiographs 🔁

  • ↑ transparency (vertebrae MORE, not less transparent ⚠), cortical thinning.
  • Spine: framed ("rim") vertebrae, prominent vertical trabeculae, biconcave ("fish") and wedge vertebrae, Schmorl nodules.
  • NOT osteoporosis: square vertebrae and syndesmophytes (= ankylosing spondylitis), increased trabecular density.
  • Regional osteoporosis: immobilisation, algoneurodystrophy (Sudeck) – post-traumatic, > 50 y; visible on X-ray after 7–10 days.

Periosteal reactions 🔁🔁

TypeMeaning
Solid, thick, unilamellarbenign, slow process
Lamellated / "onion bulb" (multilamellar)aggressive – Ewing sarcoma, malignant tumour
Spiculated / sunburstaggressive – osteosarcoma (also Ewing)
Codman trianglemalignant primary bone tumour (osteosarcoma) – not metastasis, not benign tumour

Benign vs aggressive lesion

  • Benign: sharp sclerotic margin, narrow zone of transition, intact or expanded cortex, solid or no periosteal reaction.
  • Aggressive: ill-defined, permeative/moth-eaten, cortical destruction, interrupted periosteal reaction, soft-tissue mass.
